title: Introduction to voipred
text: voipred (package voipred.dev) evaluates clinical prediction models validation sample clinical utility, quantifies much remaining uncertainty matters decision whether use . implements decision curve analysis based net benefit (Vickers Elkin 2006; Vickers, Van Calster, Steyerberg 2019), binary, survival competing-risk outcomes (Vickers et al. 2008), Bayesian framework (Wynants et al. 2018; Cruz Korthauer 2025), value--information (VoI) analysis model validation (Sadatsafavi et al. 2023, 2025). Net benefit. prediction model used decide treatment treating patients whose predicted risk threshold tt. net benefit NB=TPn−FPn⋅t1−t,NB = \frac{TP}{n} - \frac{FP}{n} \cdot \frac{t}{1-t}, proportion true positives minus proportion false positives, weighted odds threshold. threshold expresses harm unnecessary treatment weighed benefit necessary one: t=10%t = 10\%, treating 9 patients unnecessarily accepted treat 1 patient needs . Net benefit units true positives: 0.03 means 3 net true positives per 100 patients, .e. 3 patients correctly treated per 100, without unnecessary treatments. model useful threshold net benefit higher default strategies, treating everyone treating one; decision curve shows range thresholds. Value information. validation sample finite, estimated net benefit uncertain, strategy looks best (model, treating everyone treating one) may best population. VoI analysis asks much uncertainty matters decision: expected value perfect information (EVPI) expected loss net benefit due , expected value sample information (EVSI) expected gain validation study given size. complemented probability model useful, P(useful), probability strategy best, P(best). Workflow. main function nb_val(), computes net benefit one several models range thresholds. result used VoI functions: Every result print() (short table), summary() (main findings), plot() .data.frame() (full results) methods. need. patient validation sample: predicted risk event, model software (fitted model ), observed outcome: 0/1 binary outcome, time status survival competing-risk outcome.

title: voipred: value of information for clinical prediction models
text: voipred (R package voipred.dev) evaluates clinical prediction models validation sample clinical utility, quantifies much remaining uncertainty matters decision whether use . Net benefit decision curves (nb_val()), binary, survival competing-risk outcomes, one model several compared patients; Kaplan-Meier conditional inverse probability censoring weights (cIPCW) informative censoring. Value--information analysis: expected value perfect information (EVPI), probability model useful strategy best (evpi()), expected value sample information validation study (evsi()). the predicted risks of death by 5 years sf <- survfit(cox, newdata = df_val_survival) df_val_survival$p5 <- 1 - summary(sf, times = 5)$surv[1, ]  # usually only the covariates of the censoring are needed (no cipcw_control()) nb_val(data = df_val_survival,        predicted_risk = df_val_survival$p5,        outcome = ~ Surv(years, death),        horizon = 5,        thresholds = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3),        cipcw = ~ age + nodes + grade) #> Net benefit of p5: survival, horizon 5, n = 1482, risk by horizon 47.9%, censoring cIPCW (coxph), prior improper Beta(0, 0) #>  #>  threshold model NB_model NB_all NB_none delta_NB #>        0.1    p5   0.1076 0.4206       0  -0.3130 #>        0.2    p5   0.0340 0.3482       0  -0.3142 #>        0.3    p5   0.0159 0.2550       0  -0.2391  # the same covariates, truncated at 0.05 instead of 0.02 nb_val(data = df_val_survival,        predicted_risk = df_val_survival$p5,        outcome = ~ Surv(years, death),        horizon = 5,        thresholds = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3),        cipcw = cipcw_control(~ age + nodes + grade, min_prob = 0.05)) #> Net benefit of p5: survival, horizon 5, n = 1482, risk by horizon 47.9%, censoring cIPCW (coxph), prior improper Beta(0, 0) #>  #>  threshold model NB_model NB_all NB_none delta_NB #>        0.1    p5   0.1076 0.4206       0  -0.3130 #>        0.2    p5   0.0340 0.3482       0  -0.3142 #>        0.3    p5   0.0159 0.2550       0  -0.2391  # your own censoring model: fitted on the validation data, censoring as the # event, here without truncation cens_fit <- coxph(Surv(years, death == 0) ~ age + nodes + grade,                   data = df_val_survival) nb_val(data = df_val_survival,        predicted_risk = df_val_survival$p5,        outcome = ~ Surv(years, death),        horizon = 5,        thresholds = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3),        cipcw = cipcw_control(model = cens_fit, min_prob = NULL)) #> Net benefit of p5: survival, horizon 5, n = 1482, risk by horizon 47.9%, censoring cIPCW (coxph), prior improper Beta(0, 0) #>  #>  threshold model NB_model NB_all NB_none delta_NB #>        0.1    p5   0.1076 0.4206       0  -0.3130 #>        0.2    p5   0.0340 0.3482       0  -0.3142 #>        0.3    p5   0.0159 0.2550       0  -0.2391  #
